by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.intervention: Vitamin E supplements (alone, or with results for vitamin E apart)

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs with a separate vitamin E versus placebo analysis of prostate cancer incidence and mortality for prevention.

question.outcome: Stroke, with ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke apart

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of vitamin E alone versus control and reported ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke separately.
Compares many vitamins, including vitamin E, against placebo but mixes in cohort studies and reports only total stroke, not subtypes.
Pooled RCTs of vitamin E versus placebo or no vitamin E, with separate analyses of ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke.
Pooled 13 RCTs of vitamin E supplements and reported ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke separately.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs of vitamin E with separate estimates for ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke.
Pooled RCTs of vitamin E for heart disease and stroke, but the abstract gives no separate ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke results.

question.population: People who already have age-related macular degeneration (AMD), or older adults
question.intervention: Antioxidant vitamin and mineral supplements that include vitamin E (such as the AREDS formula), or vitamin E alone
question.outcome: AMD getting worse, or new AMD

decisions.reason: Covers vitamin E and antioxidant supplements for AMD onset and progression, but it is an overview mixing reviews, RCTs and non-randomised studies, not a pooled RCT analysis.
Pooled RCTs of vitamin E versus placebo in the general older population, with development of any AMD and late AMD as outcomes.
Pooled RCTs of antioxidant multivitamins (mainly AREDS, which includes vitamin E) versus placebo or no treatment in people with AMD, with progression to late AMD as outcome.
Pooled RCTs of vitamin E and beta-carotene versus control for developing AMD, including an analysis of alpha-tocopherol alone.
Pooled RCTs of alpha-tocopherol and beta-carotene versus control for onset of AMD, with separate alpha-tocopherol analyses.
Pooled RCTs of antioxidant multivitamins (mainly AREDS) versus placebo or no treatment in people with AMD, with progression to late AMD as outcome.
Pooled RCTs of vitamin E or beta-carotene for preventing AMD, and of AREDS-type antioxidants plus zinc versus control for progression in people with AMD.
Included RCTs of antioxidant supplements, including AREDS with vitamin E, versus control in people with AMD, with progression to advanced AMD as outcome.
Matching question (alpha-tocopherol versus placebo for preventing AMD), but only one trial in male smokers was included and no pooling was done.
Included RCTs of antioxidant supplements, including AREDS with vitamin E, versus placebo or no treatment in people with AMD, with progression to advanced AMD as outcome.
Mostly about dietary antioxidant intake in cohort studies, and the three supplement RCTs for preventing early AMD are only described, not clearly pooled.

question.population: Adults, healthy or with chronic diseases
question.intervention: Vitamin E supplements (alone or with other nutrients, with results for vitamin E apart)

decisions.reason: Pools RCTs of vitamin E vs control on all-cause mortality, but only in healthy adults, not people with chronic diseases.
Pools RCTs of vitamin E vs control in adults, for prevention or treatment of disease, with all-cause mortality as the outcome.
Pools RCTs of antioxidants vs placebo in adults and gives a separate all-cause mortality result for vitamin E.
Pools RCTs of antioxidants including vitamin E vs placebo or no treatment in healthy and diseased adults; analyses are by antioxidant type.
Pools RCTs of antioxidants vs placebo or no treatment in healthy and diseased adults and reports a separate mortality result for vitamin E.
Pools RCTs of antioxidants including vitamin E vs placebo, but the outcomes are cancer incidence and cancer death, not death from any cause.
The title is about vitamin E and death, but there is no abstract, so it can't be confirmed that randomised trials were pooled.
Pools RCTs of antioxidants vs placebo or no treatment in adults and gives a separate all-cause mortality result for vitamin E.
Pools RCTs of vitamin E, alone or combined, vs control on all-cause mortality in adults, including people with chronic diseases.

question.population: Adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease or NASH
question.outcome: Liver inflammation and scarring on biopsy, or liver enzymes

decisions.reason: Adults with MASLD on vitamin E, but outcomes are blood lipids and BMI, not liver histology or liver enzymes.
Vitamin E vs placebo/no intervention in NAFLD with biochemical outcomes, but trials mix children and adults and some add vitamin C.
Pools meta-analyses of RCTs of vitamin E in NAFLD reporting ALT, AST, steatosis and fibrosis.
Pools RCTs of vitamin E vs placebo or no intervention in NAFLD, with ALT and AST as outcomes.
Network meta-analysis where vitamin E is one of several drugs; the abstract reports no direct vitamin E vs placebo estimate.
Vitamin E is given only together with vitamin C, compared with no treatment, in NAFLD.
Pools RCTs of vitamin E vs placebo in adults with NAFLD, reporting liver enzymes and histology.
Vitamin E vs placebo in NAFLD with liver enzymes, but pooled analysis mixes adults and children; adult results are only narrative.
Pools RCTs of vitamin E vs control in NAFLD/NASH, with an adult NASH subgroup for enzymes, inflammation and fibrosis.

question.population: Middle-aged and older adults, healthy or with vascular disease or diabetes
question.intervention: Vitamin E supplements (alone, or with results for vitamin E apart)
question.outcome: Heart attacks, strokes or deaths from heart and blood vessel disease

decisions.reason: Asks about vitamin E and heart disease outcomes, but it is a thematic review of 58 papers with no pooled analysis of randomised trials reported.
Pools 16 randomised trials of vitamin E vs controls on stroke, with a separate analysis of vitamin E given alone.
Compares vitamins including vitamin E vs placebo for stroke, but pools cohort studies together with randomised trials.
Pools randomised trials of vitamin E vs placebo or no vitamin E on stroke, including a vitamin E alone subgroup.
Vitamin E is only given with magnesium in people with metabolic disorders, and the outcomes are blood markers, not heart attacks or strokes.
Network meta-analysis of randomised trials that includes vitamin E vs control for cardiovascular events and cardiovascular deaths.
Pools randomised trials of vitamin E in healthy adults for cardiovascular disease events and death.
Pools randomised trials of vitamin E alone vs controls on heart attack, including fatal heart attack.
Meta-analysis of randomised trials that reports a separate vitamin E result for cardiovascular disease events.
Pools 13 randomised trials of vitamin E for stroke prevention in healthy and high-risk people.
Reviews vitamin E trials for cardiovascular prevention, but it is a narrative review with no pooled analysis.
Pools randomised placebo-controlled trials of vitamin E on total, ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke.
Pools seven randomised trials of vitamin E vs control for cardiovascular death and stroke.
Vitamin E trials in diabetes with cardiovascular outcomes, but the analysis is split by haptoglobin genotype, a narrower group.
Pools randomised trials of vitamins and antioxidants, with a vitamin E subgroup reported for heart attack.
Pools randomised trials of vitamin E for cardiovascular deaths and heart attacks.
Pools placebo-controlled randomised trials, with separate vitamin E alone results for cardiovascular deaths and heart attacks.
Pools antioxidant vitamins (E, beta-carotene, C) together vs placebo; the abstract gives no separate vitamin E result.
Pooled overview of seven randomised trials of vitamin E for heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death.
Reviews randomised trials in healthy older adults and reports a separate vitamin E finding for preventing cardiovascular disease.
Vitamin E is added to aspirin versus aspirin alone, with one trial reporting a cardiovascular composite; the review studies supplement-drug interactions, not pooled prevention.
Reviews antioxidant vitamin trials for heart attack and stroke, but the abstract gives no separate vitamin E results and no clear pooling.
